questions.q: Why does a tracking backend need to log per-step metrics rather than just the final loss value?
options: Per-step logging is required by the W&B and MLflow APIs and cannot be disabled
A final loss number alone tells you almost nothing about whether training was stable along the way
Per-step metrics are cheaper to store than a single final value
Final metrics cannot be compared across runs
questions.explain: The full training curve lets you diagnose instability, divergence, or slow convergence after the fact, whereas a single final number hides all of that history.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff between a managed (hosted) tracking service and a self-hosted one?
options: Managed services cannot log artifacts at all
Self-hosting is always more expensive regardless of scale
Managed removes operational burden at a per-seat/GB cost; self-hosting is cheaper at scale and keeps data in-house but someone must maintain it
There is no meaningful difference between the two options
questions.explain: Hosted options (wandb.ai, Databricks-managed MLflow) cost money but remove uptime/backup/scaling concerns. Self-hosted options (W&B Server, OSS MLflow) are cheaper at scale and keep data in-house, but the team now owns keeping the infrastructure alive.

questions.q: What makes a growing run history stay queryable instead of becoming an unsorted pile of hundreds of runs?
options: Deleting old runs automatically after 30 days
Consistent tagging conventions (sweep ID, git branch, dataset version) agreed across the team
Switching from MLflow to W&B, since only W&B supports queries
Logging fewer metrics per run
questions.explain: Both W&B and MLflow support tagging and a query API, but without a team-wide tagging discipline, filtering hundreds of runs becomes a manual scroll through run names regardless of which tool is used.

questions.q: Why are model checkpoints and datasets logged as artifacts rather than attached to every metric log call?
options: Artifacts are required for a run to show up in the dashboard at all
Keeping large binary files out of the metrics database keeps it fast to query
wandb.log() cannot technically accept file paths
Artifacts are automatically deleted after each run, unlike metrics
questions.explain: Artifact stores like W&B Artifacts handle large, versioned binary files separately from the lightweight metric time series, so the metrics database doesn't get bloated with multi-gigabyte blobs.

questions.q: In the self-hosted MLflow tracking server command shown in the lesson, what two things does it need configured beyond the server itself?
options: A GPU cluster and a load balancer
A backend store (e.g. Postgres) for metadata and an artifact root (e.g. S3) for large files
A Kubernetes cluster and a CI/CD pipeline
A W&B API key and a wandb.ai account
questions.explain: The mlflow server command takes --backend-store-uri (a database like Postgres for run metadata) and --default-artifact-root (a blob store like S3 for large files), reflecting the split between metric/metadata storage and artifact storage.
